minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a liquor license hearing for Mickey Shay's over a December underage-service incident and a March after-hours incident. The board found violations on both and set a suspension after debating its length. It also reviewed the FY15 budget adjustment article for Town Meeting, announced a DPW contract settlement, and discussed solar interconnection and the water district.

what_happened.line: The Select Board found Mickey Shay's violated liquor rules twice and imposed a five-day license suspension, May 22 through May 26.
The board found a violation for serving an underage patron in December and a second for patrons present after hours in March.
A two-day and a five-day suspension were both proposed during deliberation before the five-day suspension passed; a written decision follows, with five business days to appeal.
The board recommended approval of Article 9, the fiscal 15 budget adjustment, which uses extra insurance credits to cover deficits and lessen a pavement management cut.
A three-year DPW contract settlement was announced, with a new step grid and a cost-neutral merit evaluation replacing personal leave.

why_it_matters: The suspension means the licensed establishment cannot serve alcohol on the set dates, and it shows how the board handles underage-service and after-hours findings.

Article 9 goes to Town Meeting, where residents vote on it; it decides how snow and ice and veterans benefits deficits are covered, how much free cash is used, and how much goes to stabilization and road work.
watch_next: Town Meeting vote on Article 9, the fiscal 15 budget adjustment; the board meets at 8 a.m. that day.
The written decision to the licensee, which starts the five-business-day appeal window.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the two violation findings, the suspension dates, the budget figures and the appeal decision. The one clear difference is the suspension: our minutes have a two-day suspension and a separate five-day proposal, and also lack the official vote tallies (4-1 on Article 9, 4 in favor with 1 abstaining on the suspension).
